question: Which of the following players is associated with billiards?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pankaj Advani.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pankaj Advani is a legendary Indian cueist associated with Billiards and Snooker. (बिलियर्ड्स — पंकज आडवाणी)

 

• He is the first Indian (and only cueist in the world) to win world titles in both billiards and snooker in the same format, and he has won numerous World Billiards Championship titles (both the time and point formats) as well as multiple World Snooker Championship titles.

 

• He has been honoured with the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna (2018), Arjuna Award (2004), Padma Shri (2009) and Padma Bhushan (2018) for his contribution to cue sports.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Advani hails from Bengaluru, Karnataka, and has represented India in international billiards and snooker events since the early 2000s.

 

NOTE

 

• Neeraj Chopra (Option 1): Associated with javelin throw; India's Olympic gold medallist at Tokyo 2020.

 

• Sankalp Gupta (Option 2): An Indian chess player, an International Master known for a blindfold chess record.

 

• Manish Narwal (Option 4): A para-shooter, Paralympic gold medallist (P4 mixed 50m pistol SH1) at Tokyo 2020.

question: Name an alkylbenzene widely used as a chemical intermediate in the production of phenol.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Cumene.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Cumene (isopropylbenzene) is an alkylbenzene that is the key intermediate in the Cumene process (Hock process), which is used to manufacture phenol and acetone together. (क्यूमीन प्रक्रिया — फिनोल उत्पादन)

 

• In this process, benzene is alkylated with propene to form cumene, which is then oxidised and cleaved with dilute acid to yield phenol and acetone as co-products.

 

• The Cumene process, developed in the 1940s, accounts for roughly 95% of the world's phenol production today, making it the dominant industrial route.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Acetone, the co-product of the Cumene process, is itself a widely used industrial solvent and a precursor to other chemicals such as methyl methacrylate.

 

NOTE

 

• Furan (Option 2): A heterocyclic aromatic compound (oxygen-containing five-membered ring), not an alkylbenzene, and not used for phenol production.

 

• Styrene (Option 3): An alkenylbenzene (vinylbenzene) primarily used to manufacture polystyrene plastics and synthetic rubber, not phenol.

 

• Toluene (Option 4): A simple alkylbenzene used mainly as an industrial solvent and as a precursor to benzene, TNT and benzoic acid; it is not the industrial route to phenol.

question: Fundamental Duties are contained within which Article of the Constitution of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 51A.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Fundamental Duties of Indian citizens are listed in Article 51A, contained in Part IV-A of the Constitution. (मौलिक कर्तव्य — अनुच्छेद 51A)

 

• Part IV-A, along with the Fundamental Duties, was inserted by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976, on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee.

 

• Originally 10 Fundamental Duties were listed; an 11th duty (a parent/guardian's duty to provide opportunities for education to a child between 6-14 years) was added later by the 86th Amendment Act, 2002.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Fundamental Duties are inspired by the Constitution of the erstwhile USSR and, unlike Fundamental Rights, are not legally enforceable in a court of law.

 

NOTE

 

• Article 492 (Option 1): No such Article exists in the Constitution of India (the original Constitution has only 395 Articles).

 

• Article 50A (Option 3): No such Article exists; Article 50 deals with separation of judiciary from the executive.

 

• Article 44 (Option 4): A Directive Principle of State Policy (Part IV) that calls for a Uniform Civil Code, not Fundamental Duties.

question: Which Indian religious festival has recently been included in the representative list of intangible cultural heritage of humanity by UNESCO, an organisation of the United Nations?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Durga Puja.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• 'Durga Puja in Kolkata' was inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in December 2021, at the 16th session of the Intergovernmental Committee held in Paris. (दुर्गा पूजा — यूनेस्को अमूर्त सांस्कृतिक धरोहर)

 

• It became the first festival from West Bengal and one of a growing list of Indian cultural elements to receive this UNESCO recognition.

 

• The inscription recognised Durga Puja as a festival where art and craftsmanship, religious devotion, and community participation come together, transcending barriers of caste, creed and economic status.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other Indian elements on UNESCO's ICH list include Yoga (2016), Kumbh Mela (2017), Ramlila, Kalbelia folk dance of Rajasthan, and Navroz.

 

NOTE

 

• Ramnavami, Janmashtami and Mahashtami (Options 2, 3, 4): None of these has been separately inscribed on UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list; Mahashtami is in fact one of the days of the Durga Puja festival itself.

question:
Which of the following pairs of ‘Ruler – Ruling period’ is correctly matched?

I. Sher Shah Suri – 1540-1545

II. Akbar – 1556-1605
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both I and II.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement I is correct: Sher Shah Suri founded the Sur Empire after defeating Humayun at the Battle of Kannauj (1540) and ruled from 1540 to 1545 (until his death at the Siege of Kalinjar). (शेर शाह सूरी — 1540-1545)

 

• Statement II is correct: Akbar, the third Mughal emperor, ruled from 1556 to 1605 — from his accession after the Second Battle of Panipat (1556) until his death (1605).

 

• Both dates are historically well-established and match standard chronology of medieval Indian history.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Sher Shah Suri is also credited with major administrative reforms, including the Rupiya currency system and the Grand Trunk Road's revival.

 

• Akbar is known for policies of religious tolerance (Din-i-Ilahi, abolition of jizya) and administrative innovations such as the Mansabdari system.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2 and 3 are incorrect because each of them denies at least one of the two ruling periods, both of which are factually accurate.

question: On 5 April 2022, who was appointed as the Chairman of the Union Public Service Commission?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Manoj Soni.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Dr. Manoj Soni was appointed to the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) on 5 April 2022; he went on to be sworn in as its Chairman on 16 May 2023, succeeding Dr. Pradeep Kumar Joshi. (डॉ. मनोज सोनी — संघ लोक सेवा आयोग)

 

• Dr. Soni is a scholar-academician who previously served as Vice-Chancellor of the Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda and of Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar Open University, Gujarat.

 

• UPSC is a constitutional body (Article 315-323) responsible for conducting recruitment examinations, such as the Civil Services Examination, for All India and Central Services.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Chairman and Members of UPSC are appointed by the President of India and hold office for a term of six years or until the age of 65, whichever is earlier.

 

NOTE

 

• S Raju (Option 1): A former Deputy Comptroller and Auditor General, unrelated to this UPSC appointment.

 

• Suman K Bery (Option 2): Was appointed Vice-Chairman of NITI Aayog in April 2022, not to the UPSC.

 

• Ashwin Yardi (Option 4): A corporate executive (former CEO, Capgemini India), unrelated to the UPSC.

question: The Planning commission of India has divided India into how many Agro-climatic Zones?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 15.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Planning Commission of India divided the country into 15 broad Agro-Climatic Zones, based on physiography, soil type, geological formation, climate, cropping pattern and the availability of irrigation and mineral resources. (कृषि-जलवायु क्षेत्र — 15)

 

• This regionalisation was undertaken as part of agricultural planning during the Seventh Five Year Plan (1985-90) to promote balanced and scientific regional agricultural development.

 

• Each zone groups together states/regions with broadly similar agro-climatic conditions so that crop planning and resource allocation can be tailored regionally.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Separately, the ICAR / National Agricultural Research Project (NARP) has classified India into a much finer set of 127 agro-climatic zones, which is a different (more granular) classification from the Planning Commission's 15-zone scheme.

 

NOTE

 

• 25, 18 and 20 (Options 2, 3, 4) do not correspond to the Planning Commission's official 15-zone agro-climatic classification of India.

question: Who among the following headed the National Income Committee?
solution_text:
The correct answer is PC Mahalanobis.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The National Income Committee was set up by the Government of India in 1949 to prepare scientific estimates of India's national income, and it was headed by Prof. P.C. Mahalanobis. (राष्ट्रीय आय समिति — पी.सी. महालनोबिस)

 

• V.K.R.V. Rao and D.R. Gadgil served as members of this committee alongside Mahalanobis.

 

• The committee submitted its first official report in 1954, laying the foundation for systematic national income accounting in India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• P.C. Mahalanobis is regarded as the father of Indian statistics; he founded the Indian Statistical Institute (ISI), Kolkata, in 1931 and was the chief architect of the statistical model behind India's Second Five Year Plan.

 

NOTE

 

• VKRV Rao and DR Gadgil (Options 2, 3): Were members of the National Income Committee, not its chairman.

 

• BR Ambedkar (Option 4): Chaired the Drafting Committee of the Indian Constitution, unrelated to the National Income Committee.

question: The mass number of titanium is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is 47.78.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Titanium (Ti), atomic number 22, has a standard atomic weight of approximately 47.87 u, and among the given options, 47.78 is the closest matching value commonly used for it in such objective questions. (टाइटेनियम — परमाणु द्रव्यमान लगभग 47.87)

 

• Titanium is a transition metal known for its high strength-to-weight ratio and excellent corrosion resistance.

 

• It is widely used in the aerospace industry (aircraft frames, jet engines), as well as in medical implants, due to its light weight, strength and biocompatibility.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Titanium was discovered by William Gregor in 1791 and named by Martin Heinrich Klaproth after the Titans of Greek mythology.

 

• Titanium dioxide (TiO2) is widely used as a white pigment in paints, plastics and sunscreens.

 

NOTE

 

• 44.56, 49.82 and 41.33 (Options 1, 2, 3): Do not correspond to titanium's known atomic mass and serve only as distractors.

question: The _________ Cabinet approved the country’s first-of-its-kind gene bank programme in the State.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Maharashtra.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Maharashtra Cabinet approved the 'Maharashtra Gene Bank Project' on 27 April 2022 — the first-of-its-kind programme in India for documenting and conserving the state's native biodiversity, including crop varieties, livestock breeds and other genetic resources. (महाराष्ट्र जीन बँक — देश का पहला)

 

• The project was sanctioned with an outlay of around ₹172 crore and aims to build a repository (gene bank) of indigenous genetic material to safeguard it for future agricultural and ecological use.

 

• It is being implemented in collaboration with the Maharashtra State Biodiversity Board and involves grassroots participation from farmers and local communities in documenting native varieties.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The initiative is aimed at combating genetic erosion caused by the spread of hybrid and genetically modified crop varieties, and at conserving climate-resilient indigenous species.

 

NOTE

 

• Rajasthan, Andhra Pradesh and Odisha (Options 1, 3, 4): None of these states approved this particular first-of-its-kind gene bank programme; it was a Maharashtra state initiative.

question: In which year did AEB de Chancourtois organise the elements by atomic weight, by graphing the elements around a cylinder with a circumference of 16 units, corresponding to the weight of oxygen (O)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1862.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In 1862, the French geologist Alexandre-Émile Béguyer de Chancourtois proposed the 'Telluric Helix' (Vis Tellurique), arranging the known chemical elements in order of increasing atomic weight along a helix traced on the surface of a cylinder. (टेल्यूरिक हेलिक्स — डी शैंकोर्तुआ, 1862)

 

• The cylinder's circumference was set at 16 units, corresponding to the atomic weight of oxygen, so that elements with similar properties tended to line up vertically on the cylinder.

 

• This was one of the earliest attempts at showing periodicity among elements, predating Mendeleev's periodic table, though it received little attention at the time since it was published in geological rather than chemical terms.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other early classification attempts include John Newlands' Law of Octaves (1865), Lothar Meyer's atomic volume curves, and Dmitri Mendeleev's Periodic Law (1869), which became the widely accepted classification.

 

NOTE

 

• 1860, 1870 and 1868 (Options 2, 3, 4): Do not correspond to de Chancourtois's Telluric Helix, which was proposed in 1862.

question:
A booklet released by the Lok Sabha Secretariat has listed out words and expressions that would be considered unparliamentary in both the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha.

Which of the following words is NOT declared unparliamentary?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chakkar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In July 2022, ahead of the Monsoon Session of Parliament, the Lok Sabha Secretariat released an updated booklet titled 'Unparliamentary Words 2021', listing words and phrases considered unfit for use in the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha. (असंसदीय शब्द — लोकसभा सचिवालय)

 

• Words such as 'Shakuni', 'Nautanki' and 'Girgit' (used pejoratively, e.g. for a shifty character or a chameleon-like turncoat) were among the terms flagged as unparliamentary in this compilation.

 

• 'Chakkar', however, was not included in this list of unparliamentary words/expressions.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other words that made headlines from this list include 'Jumlajeevi', 'Corrupt', 'Ashamed', 'Betrayed' and 'Dictatorial'.

 

• The booklet drew significant political controversy, with the Speaker later clarifying that MPs could still use such words in the House at their own responsibility, but that they could be expunged from the official record if deemed unparliamentary by the Chair.

 

NOTE

 

• Shakuni, Nautanki and Girgit (Options 1, 2, 4): All featured among the words/expressions declared unparliamentary in the booklet.

question: The shape of peninsular plateau in India is ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Triangular.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Peninsular Plateau of India (also called the Deccan Plateau) is a tableland composed of the old Gondwana rocks, and it is broadly triangular in shape. (प्रायद्वीपीय पठार — त्रिकोणीय आकार)

 

• It is bounded by the Aravalli Range in the northwest, the Rajmahal Hills in the east, the Gir Range in the west, and the Cardamom Hills in the south, giving it its triangular outline.

 

• The plateau is flanked on either side by the Western Ghats and Eastern Ghats, and it slopes gently from west to east, which is why most peninsular rivers (like the Godavari, Krishna and Kaveri) flow eastward into the Bay of Bengal.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Peninsular Plateau is divided into two broad divisions: the Central Highlands (north of the Narmada) and the Deccan Plateau (south of the Narmada).

 

NOTE

 

• Linear, Rectangular and Circular (Options 1, 2, 3): None of these describes the actual geographic shape of India's Peninsular Plateau, which is triangular.

question: Which of the following cities hosted the finals of IPL 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ahmedabad.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The final of IPL 2022 was played on 29 May 2022 at the Narendra Modi Stadium, Ahmedabad. (आईपीएल 2022 फाइनल — अहमदाबाद)

 

• Gujarat Titans, playing in their debut IPL season under captain Hardik Pandya, won the title by defeating the Rajasthan Royals.

 

• IPL 2022 was the first season to feature 10 teams, with Gujarat Titans and Lucknow Super Giants added as new franchises.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• In IPL 2022, Jos Buttler won the Orange Cap (highest run-scorer) and Yuzvendra Chahal won the Purple Cap (highest wicket-taker).

 

NOTE

 

• Kolkata, Mumbai and Hyderabad (Options 1, 3, 4): These cities hosted various league-stage/playoff matches of IPL 2022, but not the final, which was held in Ahmedabad.

question: In which of the following years, did Subhas Chandra Bose refer to Mahatma Gandhi as the “Father of the Nation”?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1944.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In a radio broadcast on Azad Hind Radio (Rangoon), on 6 July 1944, Subhas Chandra Bose referred to Mahatma Gandhi as the 'Father of the Nation', seeking his blessings for the Indian National Army's (INA) struggle for independence. (सुभाष चंद्र बोस — राष्ट्रपिता, 1944)

 

• This is widely regarded as the earliest recorded instance of Gandhi being addressed by this title, which later became his popular epithet across India.

 

• Bose made the appeal in the context of rallying support and legitimacy for the INA's military campaign against British colonial rule.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Gandhi is officially not conferred the title 'Father of the Nation' by the Constitution of India, as the Constitution does not provide for such a designation; the title is used only by convention and popular usage.

 

NOTE

 

• 1942, 1939 and 1941 (Options 1, 3, 4): These years do not correspond to Bose's radio broadcast in which he used the title for Gandhi.

question: The Green Revolution in India started in _______________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1960s.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Green Revolution in India began in the mid-to-late 1960s, primarily driven by the introduction of high-yielding variety (HYV) seeds, especially of wheat, along with expanded use of fertilisers and irrigation. (हरित क्रांति — 1960 का दशक)

 

• Agricultural scientist M.S. Swaminathan, working with Norman Borlaug's HYV wheat strains, played a pivotal role, along with the then Union Agriculture Minister C. Subramaniam.

 

• States like Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh were the earliest and biggest beneficiaries, becoming India's principal wheat-producing belt.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• M.S. Swaminathan is often called the 'Father of the Green Revolution in India', and was awarded the Padma Vibhushan and the first World Food Prize (1987).

 

NOTE

 

• 1940s, 1990s and 1950s (Options 1, 2, 3): None of these decades marks the actual start of India's Green Revolution, which began in the 1960s.

question: The Sattriya dance form was introduced in the 15th century AD by the great Vaishnava saint and reformer of Assam, ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mahapurusha Sankaradeva.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sattriya dance was introduced in the 15th century AD by Mahapurusha Srimanta Sankaradeva, the great Vaishnava saint-reformer of Assam. (सत्रिया नृत्य — शंकरदेव)

 

• It originated as part of the Ankiya Naat (one-act plays) performed within Sattras (Vaishnava monasteries) that Sankaradeva established to propagate the Bhakti movement (Ekasarana Dharma) in Assam.

 

• Sattriya was officially recognised as one of the eight classical dance forms of India by the Sangeet Natak Akademi in the year 2000.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Sankaradeva also composed the Kirtana Ghosha and introduced Borgeet (devotional songs) and Bhaona (theatrical performances) as part of his religious-cultural reform movement in Assam.

 

NOTE

 

• Chaitanya Mahaprabhu (Option 1): A key figure of the Bhakti movement in Bengal, unrelated to founding Sattriya.

 

• Vallabhacharya (Option 3): Founder of the Pushtimarg (Shuddhadvaita) Vaishnava sect, associated with Braj region, not Sattriya.

 

• Sant Namdev (Option 4): A Bhakti saint associated with the Varkari movement in Maharashtra, unrelated to Sattriya dance.

question: T Balasaraswati, a ___________ dancer was also an actress.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bharatanatyam.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• T. Balasaraswati (1918-1984) was one of the most celebrated exponents of Bharatanatyam, hailing from a traditional devadasi family of musicians and dancers in Thanjavur, Tamil Nadu. (भरतनाट्यम — टी. बालासरस्वती)

 

• Alongside her illustrious dance career, she also appeared as an actress, most notably in the acclaimed documentary/film work showcasing her art, and she was known for her expressive abhinaya (facial expression).

 

• She was honoured with the Padma Bhushan (1977) and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for her contribution to Bharatanatyam.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Balasaraswati belonged to a hereditary lineage of musicians going back several generations, and she is credited with helping revive and popularise Bharatanatyam in its traditional form in the 20th century.

 

NOTE

 

• Kuchipudi, Manipuri and Kathakali (Options 2, 3, 4): These are separate classical dance forms of India (from Andhra Pradesh, Manipur and Kerala respectively), not associated with T. Balasaraswati.

question: Who runs the government at the national level under the parliamentary system?
option_1: The President and Council of Ministers
option_2: The Prime Minister and Council of Ministers
solution_text:
The correct answer is The Prime Minister and Council of Ministers.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Under India's parliamentary system of government, the real executive power at the national level rests with the Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers. (संसदीय प्रणाली — प्रधानमंत्री और मंत्रिपरिषद)

 

• As per Article 75(3) of the Constitution, the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha (House of the People), which is the defining feature of a parliamentary form of government.

 

• The President is the constitutional/nominal head of state, who exercises executive power formally in the President's name but acts on the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers (Article 74).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• India follows a parliamentary system (as opposed to a presidential system like the USA) at both the Union and State levels, modelled largely on the Westminster (British) system.

 

NOTE

 

• The President and Council of Ministers (Option 1): Incorrect — the President is a nominal head and does not 'run' the government directly.

 

• The Prime Minister (Option 3): Incomplete — the Prime Minister governs jointly with the Council of Ministers, not alone.

 

• The President (Option 4): Incorrect — the President is only the ceremonial/constitutional head, real executive authority lies with the Council of Ministers.

question: Identify the INCORRECT pair.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ustad Vilayat Khan – Sarod.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ustad Vilayat Khan was a legendary maestro of the Sitar (not the Sarod), and the founder of the Imdadkhani (Etawah) gharana style of sitar playing. (उस्ताद विलायत खान — सितार, सरोद नहीं)

 

• Since he is correctly associated with Sitar and not Sarod, the pairing 'Ustad Vilayat Khan – Sarod' is the incorrect pair, which is what the question asks to identify.

 

• The other three pairs are all correctly matched: Ustad Allarakha Khan was a renowned Tabla player (also Zakir Hussain's father); Ravi Shankar was a globally celebrated Sitar maestro; Mogubai Kurdikar was an eminent Hindustani classical vocalist of the Jaipur-Atrauli gharana.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mogubai Kurdikar was the mother and guru of the noted vocalist Kishori Amonkar.

 

• Well-known Sarod players include Ustad Ali Akbar Khan and Amjad Ali Khan.

 

NOTE

 

• Ustad Allarakha Khan – Tabla, Ravi Shankar – Sitar, Mogubai Kurdikar – Vocal (Options 1, 2, 3): All three of these pairs are correctly matched, so they are not the answer to this 'identify the incorrect pair' question.

question: In 1498, Vasco da Gama, a Portuguese explorer had discovered a route to ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is India.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Vasco da Gama, a Portuguese explorer, discovered the all-sea route from Europe to India in 1498, landing at Calicut (Kozhikode) on the Malabar Coast of Kerala. (वास्को डी गामा — भारत का समुद्री मार्ग, 1498)

 

• He sailed around the Cape of Good Hope at the southern tip of Africa before crossing the Indian Ocean to reach India, becoming the first European to reach India by sea directly.

 

• This discovery broke the Arab and Venetian monopoly over trade between Europe and Asia and opened a direct maritime spice trade route, paving the way for Portuguese (and later other European) colonial expansion in India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Vasco da Gama was welcomed at Calicut by the Zamorin (ruler of Calicut); he later made further voyages to India and died at Kochi in 1524.

 

NOTE

 

• Australia, China and Japan (Options 2, 3, 4): None of these was the destination reached by Vasco da Gama's 1498 voyage, which was to India.

question: El-Nino develops in which of these oceans?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pacific Ocean.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• El Niño is a climate pattern marked by the warming of sea surface temperatures in the central and eastern tropical Pacific Ocean, and it is a key phase of the El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO). (अल नीनो — प्रशांत महासागर)

 

• It is associated with the weakening of trade winds across the Pacific, which allows warm water that normally piles up near Australia/Indonesia to shift eastward toward the coast of South America.

 

• El Niño events typically bring below-average monsoon rainfall to India, while its opposite phase, La Niña, is generally associated with a stronger, above-average monsoon.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The term 'El Niño' (Spanish for 'the little boy/Christ child') was originally used by South American fishermen to describe the warm current that appeared around Christmas time off the coast of Peru and Ecuador.

 

NOTE

 

• Arctic, Indian and Atlantic Oceans (Options 1, 2, 3): El Niño does not develop in these oceans; it is specifically a Pacific Ocean phenomenon (though it does affect climate patterns worldwide, including over the Indian Ocean region).

question: The border line which separate Indian and Pakistan is known as ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Radcliffe line.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Radcliffe Line, drawn by British lawyer Sir Cyril Radcliffe, demarcates the international border between India and Pakistan, established at the time of Partition in 1947. (रैडक्लिफ रेखा — भारत-पाकिस्तान सीमा)

 

• Radcliffe headed the Punjab and Bengal Boundary Commissions, which were tasked with drawing the boundary based on the religious demographics of the districts on either side.

 

• The line was published on 17 August 1947, just after independence, and it also separates parts of Punjab and Bengal that went to India and Pakistan respectively (with Bengal's portion also relevant to present-day Bangladesh).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Radcliffe Line runs for approximately 3,323 km, passing through the states of Gujarat, Rajasthan, Punjab, and Jammu & Kashmir along the India-Pakistan border.

 

NOTE

 

• Lahore line (Option 1): Not a recognised international boundary designation.

 

• McMahon line (Option 2): Demarcates the boundary between India (Arunachal Pradesh) and China/Tibet, drawn by Sir Henry McMahon at the 1914 Simla Convention.

 

• Delhi line (Option 4): Not a recognised international boundary term.

question: Identify animals that are NOT triploblastic.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Coelenterates.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Coelenterates (Cnidarians), such as jellyfish, corals and Hydra, are diploblastic animals, having only two germ layers — ectoderm and endoderm — separated by a non-cellular mesoglea, and thus they are NOT triploblastic. (सीलेंटरेटा — द्विस्तरीय प्राणी)

 

• Triploblastic animals possess three germ layers — ectoderm, mesoderm and endoderm — during embryonic development, with the mesoderm giving rise to organs like muscles and the circulatory system.

 

• Since Coelenterates lack a true mesoderm layer, they are correctly classified as diploblastic, not triploblastic.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Diploblastic animals also include the phylum Porifera (sponges), which are considered even more primitive (sometimes classified separately as having no true tissue-level organisation).

 

NOTE

 

• Molluscs, Chordates and Platyhelminthes (Options 1, 2, 4): All of these are triploblastic animals, possessing all three germ layers (ectoderm, mesoderm and endoderm), and hence are not the correct answer to this 'NOT triploblastic' question.

question:
Which of the following statement is correct with respect to the Shaka dynasty?

I. Some kingdoms of Shakas lasted for about 500 years.

II. The Shakas were followed by the Kushanas about 2200 years ago.

Which of the above statements are correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only I.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement I is correct: Certain Shaka (Indo-Scythian) kingdoms in India, notably the line of the Western Kshatrapas of Ujjain, endured for a very long span — broadly cited as lasting about 500 years in various branches/lineages across northwestern and western India. (शक वंश — पश्चिमी क्षत्रप)

 

• Statement II is incorrect: Historically, the Shakas (Indo-Scythians) were succeeded/overshadowed by the Kushanas in northwestern India around the 1st century CE, i.e. roughly 2,000 years ago, not 'about 2200 years ago' as claimed.

 

• The Shakas entered India from Central Asia around the 2nd-1st century BCE, establishing several regional kingdoms across the northwest and Gujarat-Malwa region.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The most famous Shaka ruler was Rudradaman I of the Western Kshatrapas, known for his Sanskrit inscription at Junagadh (150 CE).

 

• The Kushana Empire, founded by Kujula Kadphises, reached its zenith under Kanishka, who is also associated with the spread of Mahayana Buddhism.

 

NOTE

 

• Neither I nor II, Both I and II, Only II (Options 1, 3, 4): These are incorrect because Statement I is factually accurate while Statement II mis-states the actual chronology of the Shaka-Kushana succession.
